rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent curved bar mass across all four views, so it clears the hard rejection for single-view coherence. The dominant gesture is legible and the hierarchy is clear: one primary sweeping volume with a smaller notch-induced public threshold on the access edge. The green parcel is respected and the mass does not simply fill the boundary; instead it sits as a compact, site-responsive figure with a readable open side/cut. The blue access edge is answered by a visible seam/undercut at the end of the bar, though the public response is modest rather than fully generous. Programmatically, this is plausible for neighborhood living / ground-related mixed-use: it has a capacity-bearing low-to-mid rise body, an active edge cue, and a court-like articulation without collapsing into a sealed box. The section is calm and continuous, but the roof/section remains fairly generic; it does not yet strongly project terrace, daylight, or inhabited section logic, so section_program_fit is solid but not exceptional. Reference resonance is strongest with the curved community-center and courtyard/terrace precedents, while the more campus-like and facade-rich references are only partially transferable in massing principle.

warnings: The access-edge response is present but restrained; a deeper carve or stronger public void would improve street threshold clarity.

Sectional expression is still comparatively generic; if the next iteration aims for stronger neighborhood character, consider a more explicit terrace, lift, or carved court rather than only the small notch.
